title: Cory Doctorow: The people who tell you ‘AI is changing everything’ are lying
excerpt: It has become impossible to tell managers mesmerised by artificial intelligence that the tools are not, in fact, helpful. So employees just play along with the fiction to keep their jobs, writes our tech columnist
content_html:
Neoclassical economics assumes rationality. The corollary of "If you're so smart, why aren't you rich?" is "you're rich, so you must be very smart!" Thus it is that many people assume that if powerful, well-compensated CEOs insist that "AI is changing everything," well then, AI must be changing everything.

But the evidence for this "changing everything" thesis is thin on the ground. Despite a global mania that has reduced the real, pressing need for digital sovereignty to the imaginary need for nations to create "sovereign AI", no one can really articulate the case for "sovereign AI". If Donald Trump ordered Big Tech to turn off all of your country's chatbots tomorrow, nothing would change. Every one of your country's ministries and corporations would chug on with nary a hitch. Households, too, though perhaps a few of the younger members of those families would have to do their own homework again.

Contrast this with what would transpire if Trump directed his tech giants to switch off your country's Office 365 access, or to brick your Android and iOS phones, or to killswitch your John Deere tractors. Your country would effectively cease to exist. If "digital sovereignty" means anything, it means doing something about this urgent fact.)

The world is full of people who insist that "AI is changing everything" but who – when pressed – have to admit that what they mean is that they're pretty sure that AI will change everything. Eventually. After we allow it to consume all the planet's energy, carbon, water and financial resources.

Maybe.

(They're pretty sure.)

One person who's had a lot of opportunity to observe the shear between the stated business/AI situation and the real business AI situation is Nikhil Suresh from Hermit Tech, a consulting firm of "radically ethical data wizards" (that is, tech consultants). For a year and a half he has been talking to hundreds of executives — and, more importantly, their subordinates — about what, if anything, AI is doing for their businesses. The "head of AI" at a billion-dollar firm told him that his job was "totally fraudulent" – but that it was "the only promotion pathway remaining" at the organisation.

“We’re facing a coordination problem around executives being honest around the AI gains they’ve witnessed – if they co-operate, they keep their jobs. If they defect, they will possibly be fired by their embarrassed peers (who have now been implicitly called liars, cowards, or incompetents) and then replaced with someone that will toe the line anyway. If they could all admit the truth at once there might be some hope, but there is no way to coordinate that event.”

In other words, corporate leadership is starting from the premise that AI has (or will) radically change the business, and they're working backwards from that premise to find the evidence to support this article of faith.

❝

This has created a situation in which everyone has a strong incentive to lie about how much AI is delivering for their companies


Suresh describes this as a literal religious mania. In the 500-plus-employee businesses he studied, the only people who were promoted – or even spared from being fired – were people who professed "religious declarations of faith" about "the transformative power of AI". Employees who voiced honest, informed objections to AI in the workplace were passed over for promotions or targeted for layoffs.

This has created a situation in which everyone – "boards, executives, employees, vendors, consultants" – has a strong incentive to lie about how much AI is delivering for their companies. Suresh says he's seen announcements from publicly traded companies about their AI triumphs that he knows for a fact never took place.

Suresh says he's never seen a successful enterprise AI project: "Every single one – we have seen 0% success in a year and a half." Not one of their clients would face a business challenge if OpenAI went out of business tomorrow. The problem most companies struggle with is that they're "terminally bad at running software projects effectively". Adding AI to the mix doesn't solve this problem – it just adds a whole new range of ways that software deployment can fail.

Chatbots don't help. The internally facing chatbot that's supposed to help employees figure out how to navigate the business sucks because it is only as good as its training data – the business's documentation of its own processes. Businesses suck at documenting their processes. Customer-facing chatbots also suck. They either can't solve your problem, or, when they seem to solve your problem, the "solution" goes nowhere.

Suresh recounts his sole positive customer-service chatbot experience: a Mitsubishi chatbot with a natural-sounding, responsive voice politely took all the details of an automotive failure and promised him a callback. That callback never came, but Suresh is certain that Mitsubishi has logged this as a chatbot success story, even though the experience convinced him not to buy a Mitsubishi car.

He says he frequently encounters people who reflexively utter the AI catechism: "AI is changing everything." But when he presses these people for details, they admit that their organisation "does not currently use LLMs for anything, and indeed, that they cannot name a single thing that has changed other than they get some use out of ChatGPT".

This shear ("AI is changing everything"/"Well, OK, we're not using AI for anything") is so extreme that Suresh once met an exec who confessed to crafting an AI-centred strategy for a $2bn-a-year business, even though that exec "had never even used ChatGPT or any AI tool in their life”.

Some people have privately admitted to Suresh that they've embraced AI in order to earn a career-boosting corporate reputation for "thought leadership". But many other people (especially non-technical people) sincerely believe that AI is about to "change everything". As Suresh says, if you're in business with a liar, you might be able to reason with them in private – but you can't reason with a true believer.

The true believers are in charge. Suresh points out that it would be very weird for the CEO of an engineering firm or a hospital to mandate "specific procedures or building techniques without explicit agreement from the professionals on staff". But when it comes to AI, business leaders will confidently demand that the skilled professionals who perform the business's core functions use AI, even if those professionals don't think it will help.

As an aside: I remember the dotcom era, when the business press was full of articles about the conflict between CEOs and a new workforce that demanded the right to use the web on the job. Today, the business press is full of articles about the conflict between the workforce and CEOs who demand that they use AI.

Suresh describes workers who feel they have to "AI wash" their work: "They just do the work, the same way they have for decades, and say Claude did it." To add verisimilitude to this sham, they write circular processes in which one chatbot prompts another, and then the process repeats itself in reverse, for the sole purpose of consuming AI tokens to score a high rank on corporate "token leaderboards".

I want to reflect a little on two questions that Suresh's essay raises but doesn't answer. The first is why? Why are people in power such easy converts to this religious mania?

I have my own theory. The most important discomfort that powerful people experience is having ego-shattering conflicts with subordinates who know how to do things they do not know how to do. The fact that you're "in charge" is hard to reconcile with the fact that the people you're nominally in charge of tell you that all your ideas are impossible, illegal, immoral or lethal.

The other question Suresh implicitly raises is: "How can you reconcile the failure of AI in the enterprise with the individual claims of skilled technologists who insist that AI is helping them do great work?" The answer is that these AI users are "centaurs" – experienced workers who are assisted by automation on terms that they set for themselves.

Thanks to their skill and experience, these workers possess discernment, the ability to tell good code from bad, and (more importantly) good uses of code-generation tools from bad. They demonstrate the adage that worker-driven automation improves quality, while capital-driven automation improves throughput.

An automation technique that requires close supervision by skilled and experienced workers isn't going to be a raw productivity powerhouse. You don't "100x" your code this way, at least, not in the sense of firing 99 of your coders and having the remaining programmer pick up all their work. Rather, an automation tool that requires the continuous and conscientious exercise of discernment will let individual practitioners improve their work in extremely satisfying and useful ways. It's a way to spend more on operations in order to produce better outputs. It's not a way to cut your workforce, realise a gigantic saving, and still produce comparable goods and services at a far lower cost.

That is why some individual coders report such delight with their AI tools. They engage with those tools on their own terms, to improve their work in the ways that they, in their expert judgment, consider beneficial. No one ranks them on a "token-maximisation" scoreboard. No one tells them they can't do a project if it isn't "sufficiently AI". When they set out to do a project, no one makes them prove that it couldn't be "done by AI".

As ever, the most important fact about a given technology isn't "what it does" but "who it does it for" and "who it does it to."

Quantity has a quality all its own. These businesses aren't just wasting billions – they're replacing skilled workers with defective chatbots. As I've written before, AI is the asbestos we're shovelling into the walls of our technological society. Our descendants will spend generations digging it out again, and the longer the bubble goes on without popping, the longer it will take to repair the damage.

Cory Doctorow, who was born in Toronto and now lives in Los Angeles and London, is the Nerve’s tech columnist. His new book is The Reverse Centaur's Guide to Life After AI. He will be appearing  in conversation with the Nerve’s Carole Cadwalladr at Brighton Dome on 8 September; tickets are available here

sentences.zh: 在工作场所对人工智能提出诚实、知情的反对意见的员工会被排除在晋升或裁员的对象之外。

blocks.html_en: This has created a situation in which everyone – "boards, executives, employees, vendors, consultants" – has a strong incentive to lie about how much AI is delivering for their companies. Suresh says he's seen announcements from publicly traded companies about their AI triumphs that he knows for a fact never took place.

sentences.en: This has created a situation in which everyone – "boards, executives, employees, vendors, consultants" – has a strong incentive to lie about how much AI is delivering for their companies.
sentences.zh: 这就造成了这样一种情况：每个人——“董事会、高管、员工、供应商、顾问”——都有强烈的动机去谎报人工智能为公司带来了多少好处。

sentences.en: Suresh says he's seen announcements from publicly traded companies about their AI triumphs that he knows for a fact never took place.
sentences.zh: 苏雷什说，他看到过上市公司关于其人工智能胜利的公告，但他知道事实从未发生过。

blocks.html_en: Suresh says he's never seen a successful enterprise AI project: "Every single one – we have seen 0% success in a year and a half." Not one of their clients would face a business challenge if OpenAI went out of business tomorrow. The problem most companies struggle with is that they're "terminally bad at running software projects effectively". Adding AI to the mix doesn't solve this problem – it just adds a whole new range of ways that software deployment can fail.

sentences.en: Suresh says he's never seen a successful enterprise AI project: "Every single one – we have seen 0% success in a year and a half."
sentences.zh: Suresh 表示，他从未见过成功的企业人工智能项目：“每一个项目——我们在一年半的时间里都看到了 0% 的成功。”

sentences.en: Not one of their clients would face a business challenge if OpenAI went out of business tomorrow.
sentences.zh: 如果 OpenAI 明天倒闭，他们的客户中没有一个会面临业务挑战。

sentences.en: The problem most companies struggle with is that they're "terminally bad at running software projects effectively".
sentences.zh: 大多数公司面临的问题是他们“在有效运行软件项目方面表现不佳”。

sentences.en: Adding AI to the mix doesn't solve this problem – it just adds a whole new range of ways that software deployment can fail.
sentences.zh: 添加人工智能并不能解决这个问题——它只是增加了软件部署失败的一系列全新方式。

blocks.html_en: Chatbots don't help. The internally facing chatbot that's supposed to help employees figure out how to navigate the business sucks because it is only as good as its training data – the business's documentation of its own processes. Businesses suck at documenting their processes. Customer-facing chatbots also suck. They either can't solve your problem, or, when they seem to solve your problem, the "solution" goes nowhere.

sentences.en: Chatbots don't help.
sentences.zh: 聊天机器人没有帮助。

sentences.en: The internally facing chatbot that's supposed to help employees figure out how to navigate the business sucks because it is only as good as its training data – the business's documentation of its own processes.
sentences.zh: 面向内部的聊天机器人本应帮助员工弄清楚如何驾驭业务，但它很糟糕，因为它的好坏取决于它的培训数据——企业自身流程的文档。

sentences.en: Businesses suck at documenting their processes.
sentences.zh: 企业不擅长记录其流程。

sentences.en: Customer-facing chatbots also suck.
sentences.zh: 面向客户的聊天机器人也很糟糕。

sentences.en: They either can't solve your problem, or, when they seem to solve your problem, the "solution" goes nowhere.
sentences.zh: 他们要么无法解决你的问题，要么当他们看似解决了你的问题时，“解决方案”却毫无用处。

blocks.html_en: Suresh recounts his sole positive customer-service chatbot experience: a Mitsubishi chatbot with a natural-sounding, responsive voice politely took all the details of an automotive failure and promised him a callback. That callback never came, but Suresh is certain that Mitsubishi has logged this as a chatbot success story, even though the experience convinced him not to buy a Mitsubishi car.

sentences.en: Suresh recounts his sole positive customer-service chatbot experience: a Mitsubishi chatbot with a natural-sounding, responsive voice politely took all the details of an automotive failure and promised him a callback.
sentences.zh: 苏雷什讲述了他唯一一次积极的客户服务聊天机器人体验：一个三菱聊天机器人，声音自然，反应灵敏，礼貌地记录了汽车故障的所有细节，并答应给他回电。

sentences.en: That callback never came, but Suresh is certain that Mitsubishi has logged this as a chatbot success story, even though the experience convinced him not to buy a Mitsubishi car.
sentences.zh: 虽然这种回调从未到来，但苏雷什确信三菱已将其记录为聊天机器人的成功故事，尽管这次经历说服了他不要购买三菱汽车。

blocks.html_en: He says he frequently encounters people who reflexively utter the AI catechism: "AI is changing everything." But when he presses these people for details, they admit that their organisation "does not currently use LLMs for anything, and indeed, that they cannot name a single thing that has changed other than they get some use out of ChatGPT".

sentences.en: He says he frequently encounters people who reflexively utter the AI catechism: "AI is changing everything."
sentences.zh: 他说，他经常遇到那些本能地说出人工智能教义问答的人：“人工智能正在改变一切。”

sentences.en: But when he presses these people for details, they admit that their organisation "does not currently use LLMs for anything, and indeed, that they cannot name a single thing that has changed other than they get some use out of ChatGPT".
sentences.zh: 但当他向这些人追问细节时，他们承认他们的组织“目前没有使用 LLM 做任何事情，事实上，除了从 ChatGPT 中得到一些用途之外，他们无法说出任何已发生变化的事情”。

blocks.html_en: This shear ("AI is changing everything"/"Well, OK, we're not using AI for anything") is so extreme that Suresh once met an exec who confessed to crafting an AI-centred strategy for a $2bn-a-year business, even though that exec "had never even used ChatGPT or any AI tool in their life”.

sentences.en: This shear ("AI is changing everything"/"Well, OK, we're not using AI for anything") is so extreme that Suresh once met an exec who confessed to crafting an AI-centred strategy for a $2bn-a-year business, even though that exec "had never even used ChatGPT or any AI tool in their life”.
sentences.zh: 这种剪切（“人工智能正在改变一切”/“好吧，我们没有使用人工智能做任何事情”）是如此极端，以至于苏雷什曾经遇到过一位高管，他承认为一家年营业额 20 亿美元的企业制定了以人工智能为中心的战略，尽管这位高管“一生中从未使用过 ChatGPT 或任何人工智能工具”。

blocks.html_en: Some people have privately admitted to Suresh that they've embraced AI in order to earn a career-boosting corporate reputation for "thought leadership". But many other people (especially non-technical people) sincerely believe that AI is about to "change everything". As Suresh says, if you're in business with a liar, you might be able to reason with them in private – but you can't reason with a true believer.

sentences.en: Some people have privately admitted to Suresh that they've embraced AI in order to earn a career-boosting corporate reputation for "thought leadership".
sentences.zh: 有些人私下向苏雷什承认，他们拥抱人工智能是为了赢得“思想领导力”的企业职业声誉。

sentences.en: But many other people (especially non-technical people) sincerely believe that AI is about to "change everything".
sentences.zh: 但许多其他人（尤其是非技术人员）真诚地相信人工智能即将“改变一切”。

sentences.en: As Suresh says, if you're in business with a liar, you might be able to reason with them in private – but you can't reason with a true believer.
sentences.zh: 正如苏雷什所说，如果你与骗子打交道，你也许可以私下与他们讲道理，但你无法与真正的信徒讲道理。

blocks.html_en: The true believers are in charge. Suresh points out that it would be very weird for the CEO of an engineering firm or a hospital to mandate "specific procedures or building techniques without explicit agreement from the professionals on staff". But when it comes to AI, business leaders will confidently demand that the skilled professionals who perform the business's core functions use AI, even if those professionals don't think it will help.

sentences.en: The true believers are in charge.
sentences.zh: 真正的信徒负责。

sentences.en: Suresh points out that it would be very weird for the CEO of an engineering firm or a hospital to mandate "specific procedures or building techniques without explicit agreement from the professionals on staff".
sentences.zh: 苏雷什指出，工程公司或医院的首席执行官在没有得到专业人士明确同意的情况下强制要求“特定程序或建筑技术”是非常奇怪的。

sentences.en: But when it comes to AI, business leaders will confidently demand that the skilled professionals who perform the business's core functions use AI, even if those professionals don't think it will help.
sentences.zh: 但当谈到人工智能时，企业领导者会自信地要求执行企业核心职能的熟练专业人员使用人工智能，即使这些专业人员认为这没有帮助。

blocks.html_en: As an aside: I remember the dotcom era, when the business press was full of articles about the conflict between CEOs and a new workforce that demanded the right to use the web on the job. Today, the business press is full of articles about the conflict between the workforce and CEOs who demand that they use AI.

sentences.en: As an aside: I remember the dotcom era, when the business press was full of articles about the conflict between CEOs and a new workforce that demanded the right to use the web on the job.
sentences.zh: 顺便说一句：我记得互联网时代，当时商业媒体上充斥着关于首席执行官和新员工之间冲突的文章，这些员工要求在工作中使用网络的权利。

sentences.en: Today, the business press is full of articles about the conflict between the workforce and CEOs who demand that they use AI.
sentences.zh: 如今，商业媒体充斥着关于员工与要求使用人工智能的首席执行官之间冲突的文章。

blocks.html_en: Suresh describes workers who feel they have to "AI wash" their work: "They just do the work, the same way they have for decades, and say Claude did it." To add verisimilitude to this sham, they write circular processes in which one chatbot prompts another, and then the process repeats itself in reverse, for the sole purpose of consuming AI tokens to score a high rank on corporate "token leaderboards".

sentences.en: Suresh describes workers who feel they have to "AI wash" their work: "They just do the work, the same way they have for decades, and say Claude did it."
sentences.zh: 苏雷什描述了那些觉得自己必须“人工智能清洗”工作的工人：“他们只是做工作，就像几十年来一样，然后说克劳德做到了。”

sentences.en: To add verisimilitude to this sham, they write circular processes in which one chatbot prompts another, and then the process repeats itself in reverse, for the sole purpose of consuming AI tokens to score a high rank on corporate "token leaderboards".
sentences.zh: 为了让这个骗局更加真实，他们编写了循环流程，其中一个聊天机器人提示另一个聊天机器人，然后该过程反向重复，其唯一目的是消费人工智能代币，以在企业“代币排行榜”上获得高排名。

blocks.html_en: I want to reflect a little on two questions that Suresh's essay raises but doesn't answer. The first is why? Why are people in power such easy converts to this religious mania?

sentences.en: I want to reflect a little on two questions that Suresh's essay raises but doesn't answer.
sentences.zh: 我想稍微思考一下苏雷什的文章提出但没有回答的两个问题。

sentences.en: The first is why?
sentences.zh: 第一个是为什么？

sentences.en: Why are people in power such easy converts to this religious mania?
sentences.zh: 为什么当权者如此容易皈依这种宗教狂热？

blocks.html_en: I have my own theory. The most important discomfort that powerful people experience is having ego-shattering conflicts with subordinates who know how to do things they do not know how to do. The fact that you're "in charge" is hard to reconcile with the fact that the people you're nominally in charge of tell you that all your ideas are impossible, illegal, immoral or lethal.

sentences.en: I have my own theory.
sentences.zh: 我有自己的理论。

sentences.en: The most important discomfort that powerful people experience is having ego-shattering conflicts with subordinates who know how to do things they do not know how to do.
sentences.zh: 有权有势的人经历的最重要的不适是与知道如何做他们不知道如何做的事情的下属发生自我毁灭的冲突。

sentences.en: The fact that you're "in charge" is hard to reconcile with the fact that the people you're nominally in charge of tell you that all your ideas are impossible, illegal, immoral or lethal.
sentences.zh: 你“负责”的事实与你名义上负责的人告诉你你所有的想法都是不可能的、非法的、不道德的或致命的事实是很难调和的。

blocks.html_en: The other question Suresh implicitly raises is: "How can you reconcile the failure of AI in the enterprise with the individual claims of skilled technologists who insist that AI is helping them do great work?" The answer is that these AI users are "centaurs" – experienced workers who are assisted by automation on terms that they set for themselves.

sentences.en: The other question Suresh implicitly raises is: "How can you reconcile the failure of AI in the enterprise with the individual claims of skilled technologists who insist that AI is helping them do great work?"
sentences.zh: 苏雷什隐含地提出的另一个问题是：“如何将人工智能在企业中的失败与那些坚称人工智能正在帮助他们完成出色工作的熟练技术人员的个人主张调和起来？”

sentences.en: The answer is that these AI users are "centaurs" – experienced workers who are assisted by automation on terms that they set for themselves.
sentences.zh: 答案是，这些人工智能用户是“半人马”——经验丰富的工人，他们按照自己设定的条件接受自动化的帮助。

blocks.html_en: Thanks to their skill and experience, these workers possess discernment, the ability to tell good code from bad, and (more importantly) good uses of code-generation tools from bad. They demonstrate the adage that worker-driven automation improves quality, while capital-driven automation improves throughput.

sentences.en: Thanks to their skill and experience, these workers possess discernment, the ability to tell good code from bad, and (more importantly) good uses of code-generation tools from bad.
sentences.zh: 由于他们的技能和经验，这些工作人员拥有洞察力、区分好代码和坏代码的能力，以及（更重要的是）代码生成工具的良好使用和坏代码生成工具的使用。

sentences.en: They demonstrate the adage that worker-driven automation improves quality, while capital-driven automation improves throughput.
sentences.zh: 他们证明了一句格言：工人驱动的自动化可以提高质量，而资本驱动的自动化可以提高吞吐量。

blocks.html_en: An automation technique that requires close supervision by skilled and experienced workers isn't going to be a raw productivity powerhouse. You don't "100x" your code this way, at least, not in the sense of firing 99 of your coders and having the remaining programmer pick up all their work. Rather, an automation tool that requires the continuous and conscientious exercise of discernment will let individual practitioners improve their work in extremely satisfying and useful ways. It's a way to spend more on operations in order to produce better outputs. It's not a way to cut your workforce, realise a gigantic saving, and still produce comparable goods and services at a far lower cost.

sentences.en: An automation technique that requires close supervision by skilled and experienced workers isn't going to be a raw productivity powerhouse.
sentences.zh: 需要熟练且经验丰富的工人密切监督的自动化技术不会成为原始生产力的动力源。

sentences.en: You don't "100x" your code this way, at least, not in the sense of firing 99 of your coders and having the remaining programmer pick up all their work.
sentences.zh: 你不会以这种方式“100x”你的代码，至少，不是解雇 99 名程序员并让剩下的程序员接手他们的所有工作。

sentences.en: Rather, an automation tool that requires the continuous and conscientious exercise of discernment will let individual practitioners improve their work in extremely satisfying and useful ways.
sentences.zh: 相反，需要持续认真地运用洞察力的自动化工具将使个体从业者以极其令人满意和有用的方式改进他们的工作。

sentences.en: It's a way to spend more on operations in order to produce better outputs.
sentences.zh: 这是一种在运营上投入更多资金以产生更好产出的方法。

sentences.en: It's not a way to cut your workforce, realise a gigantic saving, and still produce comparable goods and services at a far lower cost.
sentences.zh: 这并不是一种削减劳动力、实现巨大节省、并且仍然以低得多的成本生产同类商品和服务的方法。

blocks.html_en: That is why some individual coders report such delight with their AI tools. They engage with those tools on their own terms, to improve their work in the ways that they, in their expert judgment, consider beneficial. No one ranks them on a "token-maximisation" scoreboard. No one tells them they can't do a project if it isn't "sufficiently AI". When they set out to do a project, no one makes them prove that it couldn't be "done by AI".

sentences.en: That is why some individual coders report such delight with their AI tools.
sentences.zh: 这就是为什么一些个人程序员对他们的人工智能工具感到如此满意。

sentences.en: They engage with those tools on their own terms, to improve their work in the ways that they, in their expert judgment, consider beneficial.
sentences.zh: 他们按照自己的方式使用这些工具，以他们根据专家判断认为有益的方式改进他们的工作。

sentences.en: No one ranks them on a "token-maximisation" scoreboard.
sentences.zh: 没有人在“代币最大化”记分牌上对它们进行排名。

sentences.en: No one tells them they can't do a project if it isn't "sufficiently AI".
sentences.zh: 没有人告诉他们，如果一个项目不是“足够的人工智能”，他们就不能做这个项目。

sentences.en: When they set out to do a project, no one makes them prove that it couldn't be "done by AI".
sentences.zh: 当他们开始做一个项目时，没有人让他们证明它不能“由人工智能完成”。

blocks.html_en: As ever, the most important fact about a given technology isn't "what it does" but "who it does it for" and "who it does it to."

sentences.en: As ever, the most important fact about a given technology isn't "what it does" but "who it does it for" and "who it does it to."
sentences.zh: 一如既往，关于某项技术最重要的事实不是“它做什么”，而是“它为谁做”和“它为谁做”。

blocks.html_en: Quantity has a quality all its own. These businesses aren't just wasting billions – they're replacing skilled workers with defective chatbots. As I've written before, AI is the asbestos we're shovelling into the walls of our technological society. Our descendants will spend generations digging it out again, and the longer the bubble goes on without popping, the longer it will take to repair the damage.

sentences.en: Quantity has a quality all its own.
sentences.zh: 数量本身就有质量。

sentences.en: These businesses aren't just wasting billions – they're replacing skilled workers with defective chatbots.
sentences.zh: 这些企业不仅浪费了数十亿美元，而且还用有缺陷的聊天机器人取代了技术工人。

sentences.en: As I've written before, AI is the asbestos we're shovelling into the walls of our technological society.
sentences.zh: 正如我之前所写，人工智能是我们铲入技术社会墙壁的石棉。

sentences.en: Our descendants will spend generations digging it out again, and the longer the bubble goes on without popping, the longer it will take to repair the damage.
sentences.zh: 我们的后代将花费几代人的时间再次将其挖掘出来，而泡沫持续不破裂的时间越长，修复损害所需的时间就越长。

sentences.en: Cory Doctorow, who was born in Toronto and now lives in Los Angeles and London, is the Nerve’s tech columnist.

sentences.en: His new book is The Reverse Centaur's Guide to Life After AI.
sentences.zh: 他的新书是《The Reverse Centaur's Guide to Life After AI》。

sentences.en: He will be appearing in conversation with the Nerve’s Carole Cadwalladr at Brighton Dome on 8 September; tickets are available here

sentences.en: The Nerve is a fearless, independent media title launched by five former Guardian / Observer journalists: investigative journalist Carole Cadwalladr, editors Sarah Donaldson, Jane Ferguson and Imogen Carter and creative director Lynsey Irvine.
sentences.zh: 《神经》是一个无所畏惧的独立媒体标题，由五位前《卫报》/《观察家报》记者发起：调查记者卡罗尔·卡德瓦拉德尔、编辑莎拉·唐纳森、简·弗格森和伊莫金·卡特以及创意总监林赛·欧文。

content_html_zh:
新古典经济学假定理性。 “如果你这么聪明，为什么你不富有？”的推论。 就是“你很有钱，所以你一定很聪明！” 因此，许多人认为，如果有权有势、薪酬丰厚的首席执行官坚持认为“人工智能正在改变一切”，那么人工智能一定会改变一切。

但支持这一“改变一切”论点的证据却很薄弱。 尽管全球狂热已经将数字主权的真实迫切需求降低为各国创造“主权人工智能”的想象需求，但没有人能够真正阐明“主权人工智能”的理由。 如果唐纳德·特朗普明天命令大型科技公司关闭你们国家的所有聊天机器人，什么都不会改变。 你们国家的每一个部委和公司都会顺利进行。 家庭也是如此，尽管这些家庭中的一些年轻成员可能不得不再次做自己的家庭作业。

将此与如果特朗普指示他的科技巨头关闭您所在国家的 Office 365 访问，或者砖砌您的 Android 和 iOS 手机，或者杀死您的约翰迪尔拖拉机时会发生的情况进行对比。 你的国家实际上将不复存在。 如果“数字主权”有什么意义的话，那就意味着针对这个紧迫的事实采取一些行动。）

世界上到处都是坚持认为“人工智能正在改变一切”的人，但当他们受到压力时，他们不得不承认他们的意思是他们非常确定人工智能将改变一切。 最终。 在我们让它消耗掉地球上所有的能源、碳、水和财政资源之后。

Maybe.

（他们非常确定。）

来自 Hermit Tech 的 Nikhil Suresh 是一位有很多机会观察所述商业/人工智能情况与真实商业人工智能情况之间差异的人，该公司是一家“激进道德数据奇才”（即技术顾问）咨询公司。 一年半以来，他一直在与数百名高管——更重要的是他们的下属——讨论人工智能正在为他们的业务带来什么（如果有的话）。 一家价值数十亿美元的公司的“人工智能主管”告诉他，他的工作“完全是欺诈性的”，但这是该组织“唯一剩下的晋升途径”。

“我们面临着一个协调问题，高管们要诚实地对待他们所见证的人工智能成果——如果他们合作，他们就能保住工作。 如果他们叛逃，他们可能会被尴尬的同事解雇（他们现在被含蓄地称为骗子、胆小鬼或无能者），然后被无论如何都会遵守规则的人取代。 如果他们都能同时承认真相，也许还有一些希望，但没有办法协调这一事件。”

换句话说，企业领导层的出发点是人工智能已经（或将会）从根本上改变业务，并且他们正在从这个前提开始倒推，寻找支持这一信念的证据。

❝

这就造成了这样一种情况：每个人都有强烈的动机去谎报人工智能为他们的公司带来了多少好处

苏雷什将此描述为真正的宗教狂热。 在他研究的 500 多名员工的企业中，唯一获得晋升甚至免于被解雇的人是那些宣称“人工智能的变革力量”具有“宗教信仰”的人。 在工作场所对人工智能提出诚实、知情的反对意见的员工会被排除在晋升或裁员的对象之外。

这就造成了这样一种情况：每个人——“董事会、高管、员工、供应商、顾问”——都有强烈的动机去谎报人工智能为公司带来了多少好处。 苏雷什说，他看到过上市公司关于其人工智能胜利的公告，但他知道事实从未发生过。

Suresh 表示，他从未见过成功的企业人工智能项目：“每一个项目——我们在一年半的时间里都看到了 0% 的成功。” 如果 OpenAI 明天倒闭，他们的客户中没有一个会面临业务挑战。 大多数公司面临的问题是他们“在有效运行软件项目方面表现不佳”。 添加人工智能并不能解决这个问题——它只是增加了软件部署失败的一系列全新方式。

聊天机器人没有帮助。 面向内部的聊天机器人本应帮助员工弄清楚如何驾驭业务，但它很糟糕，因为它的好坏取决于它的培训数据——企业自身流程的文档。 企业不擅长记录其流程。 面向客户的聊天机器人也很糟糕。 他们要么无法解决你的问题，要么当他们看似解决了你的问题时，“解决方案”却毫无用处。

苏雷什讲述了他唯一一次积极的客户服务聊天机器人体验：一个三菱聊天机器人，声音自然，反应灵敏，礼貌地记录了汽车故障的所有细节，并答应给他回电。 虽然这种回调从未到来，但苏雷什确信三菱已将其记录为聊天机器人的成功故事，尽管这次经历说服了他不要购买三菱汽车。

他说，他经常遇到那些本能地说出人工智能教义问答的人：“人工智能正在改变一切。” 但当他向这些人追问细节时，他们承认他们的组织“目前没有使用 LLM 做任何事情，事实上，除了从 ChatGPT 中得到一些用途之外，他们无法说出任何已发生变化的事情”。

这种剪切（“人工智能正在改变一切”/“好吧，我们没有使用人工智能做任何事情”）是如此极端，以至于苏雷什曾经遇到过一位高管，他承认为一家年营业额 20 亿美元的企业制定了以人工智能为中心的战略，尽管这位高管“一生中从未使用过 ChatGPT 或任何人工智能工具”。

有些人私下向苏雷什承认，他们拥抱人工智能是为了赢得“思想领导力”的企业职业声誉。 但许多其他人（尤其是非技术人员）真诚地相信人工智能即将“改变一切”。 正如苏雷什所说，如果你与骗子打交道，你也许可以私下与他们讲道理，但你无法与真正的信徒讲道理。

真正的信徒负责。 苏雷什指出，工程公司或医院的首席执行官在没有得到专业人士明确同意的情况下强制要求“特定程序或建筑技术”是非常奇怪的。 但当谈到人工智能时，企业领导者会自信地要求执行企业核心职能的熟练专业人员使用人工智能，即使这些专业人员认为这没有帮助。

顺便说一句：我记得互联网时代，当时商业媒体上充斥着关于首席执行官和新员工之间冲突的文章，这些员工要求在工作中使用网络的权利。 如今，商业媒体充斥着关于员工与要求使用人工智能的首席执行官之间冲突的文章。

苏雷什描述了那些觉得自己必须“人工智能清洗”工作的工人：“他们只是做工作，就像几十年来一样，然后说克劳德做到了。” 为了让这个骗局更加真实，他们编写了循环流程，其中一个聊天机器人提示另一个聊天机器人，然后该过程反向重复，其唯一目的是消费人工智能代币，以在企业“代币排行榜”上获得高排名。

我想稍微思考一下苏雷什的文章提出但没有回答的两个问题。 第一个是为什么？ 为什么当权者如此容易皈依这种宗教狂热？

我有自己的理论。 有权有势的人经历的最重要的不适是与知道如何做他们不知道如何做的事情的下属发生自我毁灭的冲突。 你“负责”的事实与你名义上负责的人告诉你你所有的想法都是不可能的、非法的、不道德的或致命的事实是很难调和的。

苏雷什隐含地提出的另一个问题是：“如何将人工智能在企业中的失败与那些坚称人工智能正在帮助他们完成出色工作的熟练技术人员的个人主张调和起来？” 答案是，这些人工智能用户是“半人马”——经验丰富的工人，他们按照自己设定的条件接受自动化的帮助。

由于他们的技能和经验，这些工作人员拥有洞察力、区分好代码和坏代码的能力，以及（更重要的是）代码生成工具的良好使用和坏代码生成工具的使用。 他们证明了一句格言：工人驱动的自动化可以提高质量，而资本驱动的自动化可以提高吞吐量。

需要熟练且经验丰富的工人密切监督的自动化技术不会成为原始生产力的动力源。 你不会以这种方式“100x”你的代码，至少，不是解雇 99 名程序员并让剩下的程序员接手他们的所有工作。 相反，需要持续认真地运用洞察力的自动化工具将使个体从业者以极其令人满意和有用的方式改进他们的工作。 这是一种在运营上投入更多资金以产生更好产出的方法。 这并不是一种削减劳动力、实现巨大节省、并且仍然以低得多的成本生产同类商品和服务的方法。

这就是为什么一些个人程序员对他们的人工智能工具感到如此满意。 他们按照自己的方式使用这些工具，以他们根据专家判断认为有益的方式改进他们的工作。 没有人在“代币最大化”记分牌上对它们进行排名。 没有人告诉他们，如果一个项目不是“足够的人工智能”，他们就不能做这个项目。 当他们开始做一个项目时，没有人让他们证明它不能“由人工智能完成”。

一如既往，关于某项技术最重要的事实不是“它做什么”，而是“它为谁做”和“它为谁做”。

数量本身就有质量。 这些企业不仅浪费了数十亿美元，而且还用有缺陷的聊天机器人取代了技术工人。 正如我之前所写，人工智能是我们铲入技术社会墙壁的石棉。 我们的后代将花费几代人的时间再次将其挖掘出来，而泡沫持续不破裂的时间越长，修复损害所需的时间就越长。
